newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris bank staff hold out against release of boss.
newsitem.headline: Paris bank staff hold out against release of boss.

text.p: The chairman of mortgage bank Credit Foncier de France continued to be held Tuesday in a five-day-old siege of the state-owned bank's headquarters by hundreds of employees.
A government-appointed mediator sought to negotiate the release of Jerome Meyssonnier but union representatives held out against his request.
"Nothing should happen as long as we're still in an active phase of this (mediation) mission," union representative Agnes Courtoux told staff after meeting with mediator Philippe Rouvillois.

Rouvillois said the release of Meyssonnier was not a pre-condition for the start of any negotiations with staff, who are protesting a government plan to shut the financially troubled home mortgage lender.
Meysonnier and seven of his colleagues have been held in the bank offices since Friday afternoon, but, after taking a more conciliatory stance initially, said Monday he considered himself a hostage.

Hundreds of employees were occupying the central lobby of the plush Paris headquarters Tuesday, many of them having spent another night sprawled across the marble floor of the giant atrium in sleeping bags.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis announced in July that part of the debt-laden group would be spun off to another cooperatively run group called Credit Immobilier, which would take on 1,500 of the staff, with the rest shunted into a new state holding company that would be closed down gradually.

He is now facing blanket media coverage of the plight of some 3,300 staff at a time of record unemployment and the thorny task of sorting out a bank which was set up 145 years ago and has a long history of providing low-cost housing loans to France's poorer families.
